subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm deciding whether this vehicle needs a skeleton at all—since it's not a creature, a static model built from plain parts should work fine, though I might add a single turret joint for a bit of articulation rather than building out a full rig.

Now I'm sketching the actual design: a boxy armored wheeled interceptor around 5.2m long and 2.3m wide, with a roof-mounted water cannon turret, neon glow light bars in cyan/magenta, and an SVG-textured corporate logo on the doors. I'm working out the geometry piece by piece—lower chassis box, wheels sized and positioned with proper ground clearance, and an upper cabin block—while planning to extrude a sloped front profile for the hood to give it some visual character.

I'm defining the side-profile outline for extrusion, with points mapping out the rear, hood slope, windshield angle, and roof, plus a gunmetal paint treatment that adds countershading and grime wear toward the bottom. Now I'm placing the wheels slightly wider than the body and adding dark wheel arch covers to tie the proportions together.

For the windshield, I'm building it as a thin tilted slab that follows the slope between the hood and roofline, giving it a slight glow and an outward-facing normal so it reads as angled glass rather than a flat panel.

Now I'm adding small tinted side window planes with narrow armored slits, positioned at x=±1.01 facing outward. I'm also placing corp decal panels on both sides using an invented security-brand texture ("VANTEX SECURITY") with transparent background and stripes, mirrored for left and right orientation.

For the roof details, I'm building a split red/blue light bar across the front, a roof rack with rails, and a rotating water cannon turret with a base cylinder, aimable barrel with a glowing cyan nozzle ring, plus feed pipes running to a rear roof tank.

I'm sizing the horizontal water tank with hazard stripe paint and an "H2O" label, adjusting its radius down to 0.4 and repositioning it so the overall roof height stays reasonable, then placing the turret just in front of it so the barrel's forward reach clears the tank.

Now I'm detailing the front end: a heavy iron ram bumper with panelling, magenta neon grille slits, cyan-glow headlight strips and a horizontal light bar across the hood, plus push-bar tubing, and finishing the rear with red taillight glow, paneled doors, and a magenta underbody strip.

I'm adding cyan underglow strips along both bottom edges, magenta-and-cyan side flank stripes, amber/blue flashers on the roof edges, an antenna array with glowing red tips, a roof-mounted sensor dome, camera pods, and detailed wheels with dark tires and glowing cyan hub rings.

Now I'm figuring out the wheel layout, going with six wheels across three axles positioned along the body length, and adding fender boxes above each wheel pair sized to fit between the body side and wheel top.

I adjust wheel positions so they sink slightly into the floor for proper contact, then shift to designing the paint scheme—going with a cyberpunk aesthetic of matte black-navy base with neon yellow, cyan, and magenta accent stripes for a riot-vehicle feel.

Writing paint shader function...

I'm planning out the texture decals — logo, windshield HUD, rear "COMPLIANCE UNIT 07" text, tank label, and a glowing rear LED screen reading "STAND DOWN," plus a roof ID decal "RC-07." I'm placing the rear screen as a plane behind the vehicle facing outward, upright and sized to fit the body width.

Now I'm figuring out the vehicle's body profile coordinates, tracing the hood, windshield, and roof as a sequence of z,y points going around the silhouette, while keeping decal planes just outside the body surface so they don't clip.

Then I'm working out window placements: the sloped front windshield's tangent and normal vectors so the glass panel sits flush with the slope, plus the grille slits on the nose and side cab windows positioned along the cab region.

Now I'm setting up helper functions for building parts—boxes and neon glow elements—along with a color palette for the car's trim.

Then I'm placing the roof light bar with alternating red/blue segments and glow boxes, plus designing a rear roof tank as a rotated cylinder with painted stripe textures.

For the tank ends, I'm using a lathe-profile for domed caps, adding thin cylinder straps around the body, and planning a curved decal plane reading "AQUA-SUPPRESS" on each side.

Now I'm positioning the tank center and adding saddle boxes beneath it, then shifting to design the turret: a short cylindrical base, a boxy housing with sloped panels, and figuring out where the barrel pivot point should sit relative to the tank's z-offset.

Working out the barrel geometry now — the inner tube, outer jacket with a cyan stripe, a frustum-shaped nozzle with a glow ring and glowing water dot, a side sight camera, and a curved pipe sweeping from the tank front to the turret housing.

Still shaping the barrel pieces...

Then I'll add a glowing ring and muzzle disk near the tip, checking that the barrel's end sits clear of the hood, and sketch a small hemisphere sensor dome on the roof, figuring out where to position it along x and z.

Now I'm placing the dome off-center with a glowing red eye, adding rear antenna rods that rise to tip height with red glow, and working out floodlight boxes near the roof corners—adjusting the light bar width so it doesn't collide with them. I'm also laying out side rail rods along the roof edges with support posts.

Then I'm adding running boards near the wheel wells, underglow strips along the flanks, and a second cyan neon stripe positioned between the wheel arches to complement the chevron paint band.

I need to adjust the fender position to avoid conflicting with the neon strip, lowering the strip to y=1.04 while keeping the fender centered around y=1.18 with a thin height. The logo plane stays centered at y=1.65, spanning roughly 1.3 to 2.0, with the chevron paint band near the wheels being mostly covered anyway. Now I'm thinking through the rear details—bumper box and dark door seam lines.

Moving to the front, I'm placing the ram-style bumper box and push bar with upright rods flanking the headlights, plus a cyan DRL strip and magenta grille slits, all positioned to sit behind or beside the bumper without visual clashes.

Now I'm adding a yellow-black hazard-striped plate across the bumper front, using striped paint on a thin horizontal box.

For the wheels, I'm building tire cylinders with dark rubber coloring, steel hubs, and glowing cyan torus rings positioned outward to suggest rim accents.

I'm adding small lug-nut cylinders arranged in rings on each wheel, mud flaps behind the rear fenders, and starting on the undercarriage/axle details.

For the chassis I'm placing a dark box beneath the body with axle rods connecting the wheels, plus cab details like camera pods with glowing lenses, side mirrors on arms, and a slim visor box with a cyan glow strip above the windshield.

Now I'm figuring out roof and hood decals: a "RC-07" plate on the roof is tricky since the tank occupies that space, so I'm shifting it to the hood, accounting for the hood's slight slope by placing the decal plane flat at a height that clears the surface without looking tilted.

For the hood decal orientation, I'm reasoning through which way the text should face—since a viewer stands in front looking at the hood, the text's top edge should point toward the back (-Z) so it reads correctly from that vantage point.

Now I'm starting to list out the textures, beginning with the LOGO texture.

Designing the logo texture...

I'm planning the remaining decals: a hazard-themed "AQUA-SUPPRESS" tank label with wave icon, a yellow "RC-07" hood ID, and dark glass textures with diagonal reflections and mesh grids for the side windows. I'm deciding which elements get glow effects (screens and HUD, not logos) before finalizing the builder export with the root part count.

Now I'm setting up helper functions for boxes, neon glow parts, and decal planes, along with coordinate utilities to keep the geometry construction concise as I add rivets, vents, door seams, and panel plates.

Next I'm defining the body extrusion with a careful outline profile ordered counterclockwise to avoid self-intersection, then writing a paint function that colors the hull based on surface normals and seam positions...

Still working through types...

Adding underglow tint and nested stripe/countershade paint logic for the tank and bumper materials, plus setting up the windshield glass with a HUD texture overlay.

Now I'm placing the rear details: glowing taillight strips, rear screen, door seams, bumper, and step geometry, then adding roof-mounted tear-gas launcher pods and skipping extras like shields and taser rods to keep it focused.

Writing launcher tube geometry...

Writing the component code now...
